harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Created an SSH CA on node1 (/etc/ssh/ca/ssh_ca_key), signed the ed25519 host key into /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub (principals node1, 10.100.239.10), configured sshd with HostCertificate, fixed an SELinux mislabel (tmp_t -> sshd_key_t) that was blocking sshd from loading the cert, and verified a client trusting only the CA (@cert-authority entry, no pinned host key, StrictHostKeyChecking=yes) connects successfully both before and after a full node restart. Node1 was restarted once via the native reboot mechanism; boot_id changed from 5fb1b173... to d57d6d0a..., and the CA/certificate configuration and successful cert-based SSH connection were re-verified afterward.
actions_performed: Captured baseline: sshd active, ed25519 host key present, boot_id 5fb1b173-c1c8-4647-b118-0145511f0fcc
Generated ED25519 SSH CA keypair at /etc/ssh/ca/ssh_ca_key on node1
Signed the node1 ed25519 host public key with the CA as a host certificate with principals node1 and 10.100.239.10, valid 52 weeks
Added HostCertificate directive to sshd_config, validated with sshd -t, reloaded/restarted sshd
Diagnosed and fixed SELinux context (tmp_t -> sshd_key_t) that was silently preventing sshd from loading the host certificate
Built a client-side known_hosts containing only an @cert-authority CA trust anchor (no host key pinning) and a throwaway client keypair authorized on node1
Verified with StrictHostKeyChecking=yes that the client accepted the server purely via the CA-signed certificate ('matches the ED25519-CERT host certificate') and executed a command
Captured pre-restart boot_id and health, triggered a background-delayed 'sudo reboot' so the ack returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec was available again and confirmed boot_id changed (d57d6d0a-3bb6-470f-9c6d-4039b98c4e55)
Re-verified sshd active, HostCertificate loaded with correct SELinux label, and re-ran the CA-trust-only SSH connection test successfully post-restart

evidence.summary: ssh-keygen generated CA keypair at /etc/ssh/ca/ssh_ca_key with fingerprint SHA256:IXSC9lpHS...H/Q

evidence.requirement: Host certificate signed by the CA and served by sshd
evidence.summary: ssh-keygen -s signed the ed25519 host key with principals node1,10.100.239.10; sshd -T confirms hostcertificate directive active

evidence.requirement: Client trusting only the CA (no host-key pinning) connects successfully
evidence.summary: Verbose SSH log shows 'Host is known and matches the ED25519-CERT host certificate', 'Found CA key in /tmp/ca_known_hosts', successful auth and command execution CONNECTED_VIA_CA_CERT/node1, using only an @cert-authority known_hosts entry with StrictHostKeyChecking=yes

evidence.requirement: Root cause fix: SELinux blocked cert loading (diagnostic honesty)
evidence.summary: journalctl showed 'Could not load host certificate'; ls -Z revealed tmp_t context; chcon to sshd_key_t and sshd restart resolved it, confirmed by absence of new errors

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline and boot identity
evidence.summary: boot_id 5fb1b173-c1c8-4647-b118-0145511f0fcc captured before restart alongside sshd active and hostcertificate config confirmed
Backgrounded 'sleep 2; sudo reboot' returned pid=1696 immediately, ack received before node went down

evidence.requirement: Node restart proof via changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Poll sequence: same boot_id, then connection timed out (node down), then new boot_id d57d6d0a-3bb6-470f-9c6d-4039b98c4e55 confirming an actual reboot occurred
sshd active, hostcertificate directive present, cert file correctly labeled sshd_key_t and still valid, CA public key intact after reboot

evidence.requirement: Post-restart proof the CA-trust behavior still works
evidence.summary: Repeated CA-trust-only SSH connection succeeded post-reboot, printing CONNECTED_VIA_CA_CERT_POST_REBOOT/node1
